Islam connects faith in Allah with worsh: Islam connects faith in Allah with worship and the way we live with others. These foundations offer a starting point for learning, one step at a time.
Quran 2:177 brings belief together with: Quran 2:177 brings belief together with generosity, prayer, zakat, keeping promises and patience. It describes righteousness through both conviction and action.
Sahih al-Bukhari 8 identifies five found: Sahih al-Bukhari 8 identifies five foundations of Islam: the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan and Hajj. They connect belief with acts of worship. Quran 2:183 speaks of fasting as a means of developing awareness of Allah; Quran 3:97 links the obligation of pilgrimage to the ability to undertake it.
Learn what you believe and the purpose o: Learn what you believe and the purpose of the worship you practise. Read the referenced passages in context, then continue learning the details with a qualified teacher.

Salah has a central place in Muslim wors: Salah has a central place in Muslim worship. The Quran connects prayer with remembrance and directs believers to seek help through prayer and patience.
Quran 20:14 joins worship of Allah with: Quran 20:14 joins worship of Allah with establishing prayer for His remembrance. Prayer is a return to that purpose, rather than only an item in a daily schedule.
In Quran 2:153, believers are directed t: In Quran 2:153, believers are directed to seek help through patience and prayer. These two are presented together: continuing to turn to Allah while facing difficulty.
Quran 2:43 calls for establishing prayer: Quran 2:43 calls for establishing prayer and giving zakat. To learn the practical details of prayer, study with a qualified teacher and ask about what you do not understand. This introduction does not replace instruction in those details.
Understand prayer as remembrance and wor: Understand prayer as remembrance and worship.
Learn the practical details with reliabl: Learn the practical details with reliable guidance.
The Quran describes itself as guidance. Reading the text, learning its meanings and considering its message are connected parts of engaging with it.
Quran 17:9 describes the Quran as guidin: Quran 17:9 describes the Quran as guiding to the most upright way and gives good news to believers who do good. Its message connects guidance with action.
Quran 38:29 speaks of a blessed Book who: Quran 38:29 speaks of a blessed Book whose verses are to be reflected upon. A translation can help a reader approach the meanings, while published tafsir offers further explanation. A translation is an explanation of meaning; it does not replace the Arabic Quran.
Choose a manageable passage. Read its Ar: Choose a manageable passage. Read its Arabic text, consult a named translation and look at the surrounding verses. Questions about interpretation deserve careful study, rather than conclusions drawn from an isolated line.

Dhikr is remembrance of Allah, and dua i: Dhikr is remembrance of Allah, and dua is calling upon Him. The Quran connects remembrance with gratitude and describes reassurance in the hearts of believers.
Quran 2:152 brings remembrance and thank: Quran 2:152 brings remembrance and thankfulness together. Gratitude gives a direction to remembrance: recognising Allah’s gifts and responding with thanks.
Quran 13:28 describes believers whose he: Quran 13:28 describes believers whose hearts find reassurance in remembering Allah. Read this verse with the surrounding passage to understand its place in the surah.
In Quran 2:186, Allah speaks of His near: In Quran 2:186, Allah speaks of His nearness and answering the one who calls upon Him. When learning a particular remembrance or dua, keep its wording, context and reported count connected to its source. A decorative counter does not establish a religiously prescribed practice.
Learn supplications together with their: Learn supplications together with their references.

The Quran repeatedly connects faith with: The Quran repeatedly connects faith with caring for others. Giving concerns the gift itself and how the person receiving it is treated.
Quran 2:177 includes giving to relatives: Quran 2:177 includes giving to relatives, orphans, people in need and travellers among the qualities of righteousness. Concern for others is presented alongside belief, prayer and keeping promises.
Quran 2:261 describes the multiplied rew: Quran 2:261 describes the multiplied reward of spending in Allah’s cause. The following verse, 2:262, praises giving that is not followed by reminders of generosity or hurtful treatment.
The five-pillars narration in Sahih al-B: The five-pillars narration in Sahih al-Bukhari 8 includes zakat. Obligatory zakat has specific rules; this short introduction is not a calculation guide. For your own obligations, seek reliable instruction about the relevant conditions.
Pay attention to people in need around y: Pay attention to people in need around you.
Protect the dignity of the person receiv: Protect the dignity of the person receiving help.
Learn the specific rules of zakat before: Learn the specific rules of zakat before calculating it.
Zakat is included among the five foundat: Zakat is included among the five foundations. Summary of the narration.
Kindness, restraint and respect are recu: Kindness, restraint and respect are recurring themes in the Quran. They reach into the home, the neighbourhood and the way people speak to one another.
Quran 4:36 joins worship of Allah with g: Quran 4:36 joins worship of Allah with good treatment of parents, relatives, orphans, those in need, neighbours, companions and travellers. Read the full verse to see the breadth of this responsibility.
Quran 3:134 praises those who give in ea: Quran 3:134 praises those who give in ease and hardship, restrain anger and pardon others. Character is expressed in the response to difficult moments as well as comfortable ones.
Quran 49:13 describes humanity as people: Quran 49:13 describes humanity as peoples and tribes who may come to know one another. It places honour before Allah in righteousness, rather than ancestry or social status.
Treat family, neighbours and people in n: Treat family, neighbours and people in need with care.
Meet people without pride in status or a: Meet people without pride in status or ancestry.
The Quran addresses hardship without pre: The Quran addresses hardship without pretending it does not exist. It calls believers towards patience, prayer and hope in Allah.
Quran 2:153 brings patience and prayer t: Quran 2:153 brings patience and prayer together. This gives a direction for turning to Allah while meeting the challenges of life.
Quran 2:155 names fear, hunger and loss: Quran 2:155 names fear, hunger and loss as forms of trial. The following verses describe the response of the patient and speak of mercy and guidance for them. Read 2:155–157 together.
Quran 94:5–6 places ease alongside hards: Quran 94:5–6 places ease alongside hardship. These verses offer reassurance; they should not be turned into a promise of a particular worldly result or a fixed deadline for relief.
Read the passages about hardship in thei: Read the passages about hardship in their full context.
Keep hope without inventing a timetable: Keep hope without inventing a timetable for relief.
The Quran calls people away from despair: The Quran calls people away from despair and towards returning to Allah. Hope in His mercy appears alongside a call to turn back to Him.
Quran 39:53 addresses those who have wro: Quran 39:53 addresses those who have wronged themselves and directs them not to despair of Allah’s mercy. This is a passage to approach with hope and attention to what follows.
The next verse, 39:54, calls people to r: The next verse, 39:54, calls people to return to their Lord and submit to Him. Reading these verses together connects hope with repentance and a changed direction.
Quran 3:135 describes people who remembe: Quran 3:135 describes people who remember Allah after wrongdoing, seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in what they have done. The emphasis includes returning and responding, rather than treating wrongdoing as unimportant.
Do not let a mistake become despair.

How Al Furqan handles your information,: How Al Furqan handles your information, account and browser data.
Al Furqan operates getfurqan.online. Thi: Al Furqan operates getfurqan.online. This policy explains how this website uses information. You can read without an account. Contact us about privacy or your information using the email below.
For an account, we collect your name, em: For an account, we collect your name, email, account status and authentication records through Supabase. The administrator can view account details and manage access. Passwords are handled by the authentication service and are not visible in the admin panel.
The contact form stores your name, email: The contact form stores your name, email, subject, message, website language, submission time and message reference. An authorized administrator uses these to answer and manage your enquiry. It does not subscribe you to marketing emails. Do not send passwords or sensitive documents.
Bookmarks, reading progress, study notes: Bookmarks, reading progress, study notes, personal reflections, remembrance counters and preferences are stored in your browser. Signing in does not sync them to your account or another device. Language, theme, sign-in sessions and prayer location settings also use browser storage; the prayer calendar cache is reused for up to 24 hours.
You can delete notes with their controls: You can delete notes with their controls or clear website data in your browser. Clearing data may remove saved reading information and sign you out. On a shared browser profile, other people may see your local notes. This website currently has no advertising trackers and does not sell personal information.
When the weekly ayah is visible, we send: When the weekly ayah is visible, we send its reference and a random browser token to count one visit per verse per day. The view-count table stores no email, account ID or IP address. Tokens older than 30 days are cleared when later visits are counted; aggregate totals remain. Hosting services may still receive connection data.
GitHub Pages hosts the public website. S: GitHub Pages hosts the public website. Supabase supports accounts, contact messages and view counts; email services deliver account messages. Quran.Foundation, QuranEnc, the Hadith API dataset and its delivery services supply texts, fonts or audio. AlAdhan receives the city, country and calculation settings you select for prayer times; we do not request GPS location.
When a feature contacts a provider, that: When a feature contacts a provider, that provider can receive your IP address, browser details and requested content. Providers may process information in other countries under their own policies. Authorized administrators and necessary service providers can access relevant records; disclosure may also be required by law. Contact us for information about applicable transfer safeguards.
We use information to provide requested: We use information to provide requested features, authenticate accounts, answer enquiries, keep the service secure and prevent abuse. Where data protection law requires a legal basis, these purposes rely on providing the service you request and our legitimate interests in operating and securing it; we seek consent where required. We do not use your reading activity to make automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Account information remains while the ac: Account information remains while the account exists. Contact messages and administrative access records currently have no automatic expiry. We retain them for handling enquiries, follow-up and security, and you may request deletion. Limited records may need to remain for legal obligations or unresolved security issues; provider backups and logs follow their own retention arrangements.
We use access controls to restrict prote: We use access controls to restrict protected records. No online service or browser storage can guarantee complete security. Keep your password private, sign out on shared devices and keep copies of notes you want to preserve.
You can update your profile name in your: You can update your profile name in your account. Email us to request access, correction, deletion or a copy of your server-held information, or to raise a concern. Depending on applicable law, you may also request restriction, object to processing, withdraw consent where used, or complain to your local data protection authority. We may need to verify your identity before acting. Local browser notes cannot be retrieved by the administrator.
Reading is open without registration. Yo: Reading is open without registration. Younger visitors should involve a parent or guardian before creating an account or sending personal information where local law requires it. If a child supplied information without required permission, contact us to request its removal.
We update this page when our practices c: We update this page when our practices change and show the revision date above. Material changes will be brought to your attention where required. Privacy questions and requests can be sent to the address below.
The conditions for using Al Furqan and i: The conditions for using Al Furqan and its reading and study tools.
These terms apply to getfurqan.online, o: These terms apply to getfurqan.online, operated as Al Furqan. Use the website lawfully and respectfully. Quran reading does not require an account. If you do not agree with these terms, stop using the service. Younger visitors should obtain parental or guardian permission where required by local law.
Translations convey an understanding of: Translations convey an understanding of the meanings and do not replace the Arabic Quran. Tafsir, hadith editions and grades must be read with their references and context. Editorial topics and personal notes are separate from published scripture and scholarly commentary. This website is a study aid, not a certified Mushaf or a personal religious ruling; consult a qualified scholar for individual questions.
We aim to display published texts accura: We aim to display published texts accurately, but errors, missing entries and differences between editions can occur. Report suspected issues with the verse or hadith reference and edition name. Do not change or redistribute source text in a way that misrepresents its meaning or attribution.
Prayer times are calculated estimates ba: Prayer times are calculated estimates based on your selected location and method, not a mosque congregation or Friday prayer timetable. Check the settings and local mosque guidance, especially at high latitudes. Hijri dates may differ from local moon sighting. Keep your own copies of notes and saved information; browser data may be lost and does not sync between devices.
Provide accurate account information, pr: Provide accurate account information, protect your password and use only accounts you are authorized to access. Do not impersonate others, send spam or harmful content, attack the service, bypass access controls, collect other users’ information or overload content providers. You are responsible for content you submit and should have permission to share it.
The administrator may suspend protected: The administrator may suspend protected account access to address misuse or security concerns. Contact us if you believe a restriction is mistaken or want to request account deletion. Public reading remains available without signing in.
Quran text presentations, translations,: Quran text presentations, translations, commentary, recitations, datasets and fonts may have separate owners and licences. Access through Al Furqan does not grant unrestricted reuse rights. Preserve source attribution and follow the relevant source licence before copying or redistributing content. You retain rights to your own notes and messages; submitting a message allows us to handle your enquiry.
Content services and external links have: Content services and external links have their own terms and privacy practices. We do not control their availability or endorse everything on linked websites. Do not bypass their restrictions.
Features may change, be interrupted or b: Features may change, be interrupted or become unavailable. We cannot guarantee uninterrupted access, complete datasets or error-free displays. To the extent allowed by applicable law, the service is provided as available. Nothing in these terms excludes liability or consumer rights that the law does not allow us to exclude.
Our Privacy Policy explains account info: Our Privacy Policy explains account information, messages, browser storage and service providers. These terms do not replace that policy or make privacy rights depend on acceptance. Updated terms will appear here with a revision date; material changes will be notified where required and will not remove rights already provided by law.
Contact Al Furqan using the email below: Contact Al Furqan using the email below for questions, text corrections, account concerns or disputes. We will review the issue and seek a reasonable resolution. Applicable mandatory law and your right to use competent courts or authorities remain unaffected.

Choosing Enable private sync gives permission to store your saved verses, reading place, daily goal, reading history, study notes and weekly reflections with Supabase and sync them across your signed-in devices. Guest data is imported only when you choose it. Language, theme, remembrance counters and prayer settings remain browser preferences; the prayer calendar cache is reused for up to 24 hours.
You can delete notes with their controls: You can delete notes with their controls; when private sync is enabled, deletions reach your account when a sync succeeds. Clearing website data removes local copies and unsynced edits and may sign you out, but does not delete information already held in your account. Contact us to request server-held data deletion. Other people using the same browser profile may access local data. This website has no advertising trackers and does not sell personal information.
Voice search starts only when you press: Voice search starts only when you press its button and allow microphone access. Your browser may send audio to its own speech-recognition service under that service’s privacy practices. Al Furqan does not record or store raw microphone audio. Recognized text fills the search box for you to review; it is sent for a Quran search only when you submit it. Arabic and English voice input depend on browser support.
Prayer times are calculated estimates ba: Prayer times are calculated estimates based on your selected location and method, not a mosque congregation or Friday prayer timetable. Check the settings and local mosque guidance, especially at high latitudes. Hijri dates may differ from local moon sighting. Keep your own copies of notes and saved information; browser-only data may be lost, while optional private account sync requires a successful connection.
